subject: PharmaLogic: Benchmark sprint charter & run coordination
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ari Gomez <ari@pharmalogic.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: PharmaLogic benchmark sprint — draft charter attached

Hi Lauren / Evelyn,

Looping you both in to start the formal handoff for PharmaLogic's benchmarking sprint. Ari and Samir have agreed to a 3-day run window next week; we need to lock the scope, pass/fail criteria, and the set of traffic mixes we'll run.

Attached is a short sprint charter I sketched (pharmalogic_benchmark_sprint_charter_v1.xlsx) — it contains:
- Acceptance thresholds (p50/p90 latency targets, 95th token latency, throughput per instance)
- Test matrix (prompt types, sequence lengths, batch sizes)
- Environment checklist (VPC peering, secrets, model variant pinning)
- Roles & responsibilities for the run days

Initial asks:
1) Lauren — confirm the acceptance thresholds and whether we should require p95 < 800ms for the primary flow or relax to 1s.
2) Evelyn — can you validate the environment checklist and flag anything that requires a config update (I attached pharmalogic_test_env_config.yml).
3) Ari — can you confirm that the test dataset (subset of anonymized prompts) will be ready by Mon 8/17 EOD?

Goal: get to a signed charter and a test-run dry run by 8/18 so the formal runs on 8/19–8/21 are smooth.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: pharmalogic_benchmark_sprint_charter_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)
Attachment: pharmalogic_test_env_config.yml (text, 3KB)

From: Ari Gomez <ari@pharmalogic.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@pharmalogic.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PharmaLogic benchmark sprint — draft charter attached

Hi Ben — thanks for the charter.

Quick answers:
- Our ops team can deliver an anonymized ~10k prompt set by EOD Mon 8/17.
- We're comfortable with p95 < 1s for the initial acceptance; if the dry run looks strong we can tighten to 800ms in a follow-up.
- We'll provide SSH access to a staging-to-redwood peering host and a service account in the morning of 8/18.

A couple of asks from our side: please add a short checklist for the post-run artifact handoff (logs, per-token latency CSV, and the KV-cache warmup snapshot). Also note that our compliance team requires that any logs handed off redact user identifiers.

We prefer the three-day window 8/19–8/21, with the first day dedicated to smoke and load ramp-up, second day to full load, third day to regression and failover tests.

I'll be on the calls during the runs; Samir will own the infra access.

Best,
Ari

--
Ari Gomez
Director, Platform Reliability — PharmaLogic
ari@pharmalogic.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ari Gomez <ari@pharmalogic.com>, Samir Patel <samir@pharmalogic.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PharmaLogic benchmark sprint — draft charter attached

Thanks Ben / Ari — quick internal notes and edits:

Ben — proposed acceptance thresholds look reasonable but suggest the following change:
- Primary flow: p50 < 150ms, p90 < 350ms, p95 < 1s (initial sprint) — we'll document tightening steps post-run.
- Token-level 95th latency: < 200ms on the production model variant; we'll record per-token histograms for analysis.

Evelyn — please verify the test environment has the following pre-warm steps included in run day 0 (8/18):
- KV cache warm-up using a 20% sample of the prompt set run at low concurrency.
- Model variant pin (redwood-model-v2.3-quant) to avoid drift during the run.
- A synthetic traffic generator config to replicate 60/30/10 short/medium/long prompt mix.

Operational run plan (proposed):
- 8/18: Dry run & access validation (participants: Redwood SRE, PharmaLogic infra)
- 8/19: Ramp to target RPS, validate p90/p95 baselines
- 8/20: Sustained full load (4h steady-state windows + spike tests)
- 8/21: Regression, failover, and artifact handoff

I'll add a small section to the charter about compliance redaction for logs per Ari's note.

Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Senior Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ari Gomez <ari@pharmalogic.com>, Samir Patel <samir@pharmalogic.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PharmaLogic benchmark sprint — draft charter attached

All — environment checklist validated. Notes:

1) config: pharmalogic_test_env_config.yml — updated two small items and attached as pharmalogic_test_env_config.yml.v2 in our internal run deck:
   - Increased Redis KV cache max memory to accommodate warm-up snapshot.
   - Explicit CORS rule for the peering host.

2) telemetry: we'll push per-instance per-token CSVs to the Redwood run storage bucket and provide a trimmed, PII-redacted CSV to PharmaLogic after the run. The run storage path will be: s3://redwood-runs/PLG-2026-0892/ (link in charter).

3) run templates: attached a simple runner command set we'll use to automate 4 concurrent generator workers and the spike scenario. We'll run the dry run on 8/18 09:00 PT and the first formal ramp on 8/19 09:00 PT — Ari / Samir, please confirm 09:00 is OK.

4) artifacts: expected post-run artifacts: per-token latency CSV, per-request JSON traces (redacted), KV-cache snapshot (gzip), run manifest (YAML), and the run logs archive.

I'll upload the updated charter and the config v2 to the shared doc shortly.

Evelyn

--
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
